Intro.title:
A voice that rises in Amed
and lands on stage.
Intro.body: Koma Amed was founded in 1988 in Ankara by medical students. It joined traditional Kurdish melody to jazz and folk arrangement, and left three studio albums in years when Kurdish was banned. In 2023 six musicians returned to the stage.

MembersPage.title: About us
MembersPage.subtitle:
Koma Amed was founded in 1988 in Ankara by medical students.
On stage today: Serhat Karakaş, Memo Gül, Serap Sönmez, Süleyman Gültekin, Fikri Kutlay and Ahmet Kaya.
Founder Evdılmelik Şexbekir (Melek) was the first album’s vocalist; he died in 1992.

serhat-karakas.name: Serhat Karakaş
serhat-karakas.shortBio: He moved from Koma Dengê Azadî to Koma Amed. A founder of Çar Newa.
serhat-karakas.quote: We have grown a little older, but our songs are still young.
serhat-karakas.story: Serhat Karakaş, known on stage as Serhat Çarnewa, comes from a dengbêj family in Doğubeyazıt, Ağrı. He studied sociology at Istanbul University in 1984. He began with Koma Dengê Azadî and joined Koma Amed in the early 1990s. After the group dispersed he founded Çar Newa with Süleyman Gültekin, Dr. Ahmet Kaya and Dr. Fikri Kutlay, appearing on Sî (2000), Mak (2003) and Ziz (2007). Able to travel to Turkey, he became a bridge in the 2023 reunion. He sang in Paris and Cologne in 2024, at Diyarbakır Newroz Park in 2025 and at Harbiye in Istanbul in 2026.

memo-gul.name: Memo Gül
memo-gul.shortBio: Joined in the early 1990s as arranger, vocalist and bağlama player; the one who announced the group’s return in 2023.
memo-gul.quote: Coming together again as Koma Amed excited us as much as it did our listeners.
memo-gul.story: Memo Gül (Mehmet Gül) joined Koma Amed in the early 1990s on bağlama and vocal, during the Istanbul MKM years. After the group dispersed he continued in Europe; in a 2025 interview he said he had lived in Europe for thirty years. On 1 February 2023 he shared the acoustic Êvarê recording and announced the reunion. He played saz and sang at Paris Cirque d’Hiver, on the Cologne live album, and at the 2025 Diyarbakır and 2026 Cemil Topuzlu Open-Air Theatre concerts. He has said his greatest wish is for every member to stand on an Amed stage together.

serap-sonmez.name: Serap Sönmez
serap-sonmez.shortBio: MKM, Koma Mezrabotan and Koma Amed. One of six vocalists of the return concerts.
serap-sonmez.story: Serap Sönmez was born in Istanbul in 1973. She began music work when the Mesopotamia Culture Center opened in 1991. In 1993 she sang solo vocal on Koma Mezrabotan’s album Kedkar. She joined Koma Amed in early 1995 and sang through the Dergûş years. She also sang in the women’s group Koma Asmin. In 2000 she wrote the music for Teatra Jiyana Nû’s play Ta and won Best Theatre Music at the 2nd Berlin Kurdish Theatre Festival. In 2005 she studied voice with Cavit Murtezaoğlu; her first solo concert was in 2006. She was one of the group’s six vocalists in Paris and Cologne in 2024, at Diyarbakır Newroz Park in 2025 and at the Harbiye Cemil Topuzlu Open-Air Theatre in 2026.

suleyman-gultekin.name: Süleyman Gültekin
suleyman-gultekin.shortBio: From Tuzluca. A founder of Çar Newa; lived for many years in Germany and Paris.
suleyman-gultekin.quote: Perhaps the thing we want most in this life is to stand on stage in Amed with every member of Koma Amed.
suleyman-gultekin.story: Süleyman Gültekin, known on stage as Süleyman Çarnewa, is from Tuzluca, Iğdır. He joined Koma Amed in the 1990s as vocalist, composer and arranger. After the group dispersed he helped found Çar Newa. He lived for many years between Germany and Paris and has said that, for various reasons, he could not easily return to Turkey. He was among those who sang Êvarê at the 2023 reunion. He performed in Paris and Cologne in 2024. With the group back in Turkey, he performed at Amed Newroz Park in 2025 and at the Harbiye Cemil Topuzlu Open-Air Theatre in 2026.

fikri-kutlay.name: Fikri Kutlay
fikri-kutlay.shortBio: A founding member, known for his strong voice as well as his career in cardiovascular surgery.
fikri-kutlay.story: Dr. Fikri Kutlay is a founding member of Koma Amed, a composer and a collector of songs. He graduated from Hacettepe University Faculty of Medicine in 1990 and completed cardiovascular surgery at Istanbul University Institute of Cardiology in 1997. He worked as an operating surgeon in Batman from 2011 to 2017 and still practises in Istanbul. Compositions such as Kulîlka Azadî, Ronahî-Berîvan, Destana Silopî and Gurbet, and collections such as Hoy Memo and Amedîye, are tied to his work. He plays accordion and cura. In 2016 Kom Müzik released Stranên Fikri Kutlay. He appeared on Çar Newa’s Sî, Mak and Ziz, and is in the 2024–2026 stage lineup.

ahmet-kaya.name: Ahmet Kaya
ahmet-kaya.shortBio: A founding member and specialist physician; not the famous singer Ahmet Kaya.
ahmet-kaya.story: Dr. Ahmet Kaya was born in Erzurum in 1968. As a Hacettepe medical student he founded Koma Amed with Evdılmelik Şexbekir and Fikri Kutlay. He sang, collected and composed on all three studio albums. He is not the well-known singer Ahmet Kaya; Koma Amed’s Ahmet Kaya is a physician who has practised in Istanbul. After the group dispersed he appeared on Çar Newa’s Sî, Mak and Ziz. From 2011 he contributed words, music and vocal to albums by Mehmet Akbaş, Agit Işık, Rewşan Çeliker and Tara Mamedova. In 2020 he composed Bildiğin Halde, from Nâzım Hikmet, for health workers lost in the pandemic, and began recording Payîza Derengî (Late Autumn). He is on the post-2024 stage lineup.

evdilmelik-sexbekir.name: Evdılmelik Şexbekir
evdilmelik-sexbekir.shortBio: A life and musical journey from Syria to Hacettepe. Melek was one of the founders of Koma Amed and is also known for the Kurdish version of Çav Bella.
evdilmelik-sexbekir.story: Evdılmelik Şexbekir is remembered as Melek or Melek Şengal. He came from Syria to Hacettepe Faculty of Medicine in Ankara. A student of painting, poetry and music, he wrote verse even though he learned Turkish later. In 1988 he formed the core of Koma Amed with Gülşen Çetin, Savaş Çakmak, Rohat Kutlay, Fikri Kutlay, Mustafa Kart and Ahmet Kaya. He was the principal vocalist on the first album, Kulîlka Azadî, and made the first Kurdish version of Bella Ciao as Çav Bella. In February 1990 he recorded in Mete Artun’s studio in Ankara Bahçelievler, in two days. In 1991, under pressure and detention, he moved to Çapa Medicine; that September he joined the armed struggle. In 1992 he died in Bitlis, aged twenty-four. After his death the group continued in Istanbul at the Mesopotamia Culture Center.

kulilka-azadi.name: Kulîlka Azadî
kulilka-azadi.description: Flower of Freedom. Recorded in 1990; widely dated 1992. Circulated first as a pirate cassette while Kurdish was banned. Çav Bella, Telli Telli; the title from a poem by Muzaffer İlhan Erdost. Lineup: Evdılmelik Şexbekir, Gülşen Çetin, Savaş Çakmak, Rohat Kutlay, Fikri Kutlay, Mustafa Kart, Ahmet Kaya.

agir-u-mirov.name: Agir û Mirov
agir-u-mirov.description: Fire and Human. Kom Müzik, 1995. Marches, folk songs and pieces in several Kurdish dialects. The Serhildan tour in Italy the same period: Rome, Palermo, Catania, Trieste.

dergus.name: Dergûş
dergus.description: Cradle. Ses Plak 1997, Kom Müzik 1998. The best-known album; period sources speak of 200–400 thousand copies. Hoy Memo, Êvarê, Amedîye, Teşî. In 1999 Foreign Minister İsmail Cem gave the album to EU ministers.

About.title:
A place’s name
becomes a voice’s name.
About.lead: Koma Amed was founded in 1988 in Ankara by medical students. The name comes from Amed, the Kurdish name of Diyarbakır.
About.p1: The core formed when Evdılmelik Şexbekir (Melek), who had come from Syria to Hacettepe Medicine, met Gülşen Çetin, Savaş Çakmak, Rohat Kutlay, Fikri Kutlay, Mustafa Kart and Ahmet Kaya. The name is tied to Selçuk Mızraklı and a house in Ankara. The first album, Kulîlka Azadî, was recorded in two days in February 1990 at Mete Artun’s studio in Bahçelievler and first copied in secret because Kurdish was banned. Şexbekir translated Bella Ciao as Çav Bella; Telli Telli, after Murathan Mungan and Manos Loizos, also helped open the studio door.
About.p2: Şexbekir joined the armed struggle in 1991 and died in Bitlis in 1992. The group moved to Istanbul and worked at the Mesopotamia Culture Center. Serhat Karakaş, Merdan Zırav, Memo Gül, Mehmet Kaya, Birkan Çelik, then Serap Sönmez, Süleyman Gültekin and Leyla joined. Agir û Mirov (1995) and the Italian Serhildan tour; Dergûş (1997) reached the widest audience. Exile split the lineup. Serhat, Süleyman, Ahmet Kaya and Fikri Kutlay released Sî, Mak and Ziz as Çar Newa.
About.p3: On 1 February 2023 the acoustic Êvarê announced the reunion. 1 June 2024, Paris Cirque d’Hiver; 5 July 2024, Cologne; 25 October 2025, Diyarbakır Newroz Park; 2026, Cemil Topuzlu Open-Air Theatre in Harbiye, Istanbul. The stage now holds Memo Gül, Serhat Karakaş, Süleyman Gültekin, Fikri Kutlay, Serap Sönmez and Ahmet Kaya. Gülşen Çetin, Savaş Çakmak, Rohat Kutlay, Mustafa Kart, Merdan Zırav, Mehmet Kaya, Birkan Çelik, Leyla and Mazlum Rewşen appear in the sources.
About.chapter1Body: Founded in 1988 by a group of medical students. The album was named that same evening: Kulîlka Azadî - Flower of Freedom.
About.chapter2Body: A journey that began at the Mesopotamia Culture Center in Istanbul continued with the second and third albums and the Italian tour. Then came exile. Çar Newa carried the music on, this time in Europe.
About.chapter3Body: In 2023 the acoustic Êvarê recordings were made. In 2024 Paris and Cologne, in 2025 Amed, in 2026 Harbiye… Years passed and cities changed, but the songs never aged. And years later, the same lineup met on stage again.
